subtopics.name: Measuring length and volume
subtopics.detail: Using rulers and measuring cylinders to find lengths and volumes; determining small distances or short time intervals by measuring multiples (e.g. pendulum period).

subtopics.name: Measuring time intervals
subtopics.detail: Measuring time intervals using clocks and digital timers; determining averages by measuring multiples.

subtopics.name: Scalars and vectors
subtopics.detail: Difference between scalar (magnitude only) and vector (magnitude + direction) quantities. Scalars: distance, speed, time, mass, energy, temperature. Vectors: force, weight, velocity, acceleration, momentum, electric and gravitational field strength.

subtopics.name: Resultant of perpendicular vectors
subtopics.detail: Determining by calculation or graphically the resultant of two vectors at right angles (forces or velocities only).

subtopics.name: Speed and velocity
subtopics.detail: Speed = distance / time; velocity = speed in a given direction. Average speed = total distance / total time.

subtopics.name: Acceleration and deceleration
subtopics.detail: Acceleration = change in velocity / time. Deceleration is negative acceleration. Uniform and non-uniform acceleration.

subtopics.name: Distance-time graphs
subtopics.detail: Sketching, plotting and interpreting distance-time graphs. Gradient of a straight-line section gives speed.

subtopics.name: Speed-time graphs
subtopics.detail: Sketching, plotting and interpreting speed-time graphs. Gradient gives acceleration; area under graph gives distance. Identifying constant and changing acceleration.

subtopics.name: Acceleration of free fall
subtopics.detail: The acceleration of free fall g near Earth's surface is approximately constant (~10 m/s²).

subtopics.name: Free fall and terminal velocity
subtopics.detail: Motion of objects falling in a uniform gravitational field with and without air/liquid resistance, including terminal velocity.

subtopics.name: Mass and weight
subtopics.detail: Mass is the quantity of matter; weight is the gravitational force on a mass. Both measured with a balance.

subtopics.name: Gravitational field strength
subtopics.detail: g = W/m; equivalent to acceleration of free fall. g ≈ 10 N/kg near Earth's surface.

subtopics.name: Density definition and equation
subtopics.detail: Density = mass / volume (ρ = m/V). Units: kg/m³ or g/cm³.

subtopics.name: Measuring density experimentally
subtopics.detail: Determining density of a liquid, regularly shaped solid, and irregularly shaped solid (volume by displacement).

subtopics.name: Floating and sinking
subtopics.detail: Whether an object or liquid floats based on density comparisons (for liquids that do not mix).

subtopics.name: Effects of forces and deformation
subtopics.detail: Forces may change size and shape of an object. Load-extension graphs for elastic solids; associated experimental procedures.

subtopics.name: Hooke's Law and spring constant
subtopics.detail: Spring constant k = F/x. Limit of proportionality: where load-extension graph ceases to be straight.

subtopics.name: Resultant forces
subtopics.detail: Resultant of two or more forces along the same straight line; resultant of forces at right angles.

subtopics.name: Newton's Laws of motion
subtopics.detail: Newton's 1st Law: object stays at rest or uniform motion unless acted on by a resultant force. Newton's 2nd Law: F = ma.

subtopics.name: Friction and drag
subtopics.detail: Solid friction impedes motion and produces heating. Drag (fluid friction) acts on objects moving through a liquid or gas.

subtopics.name: Moments and turning effects
subtopics.detail: Moment = force × perpendicular distance from pivot. Everyday examples of turning effects.

subtopics.name: Principle of moments
subtopics.detail: For a body in equilibrium: sum of clockwise moments = sum of anticlockwise moments. Applied to one or more forces each side of the pivot.

subtopics.name: Centre of gravity and equilibrium
subtopics.detail: Centre of gravity: point where weight acts. Experiment to find it for an irregular lamina. No resultant moment on an object in equilibrium.

topics.name: Momentum
keywords: resultant force acting for a time

subtopics.name: Momentum definition
subtopics.detail: Momentum p = mv. Unit: kg m/s.

subtopics.name: Conservation of momentum
subtopics.detail: Principle of conservation of momentum applied to simple one-dimensional collision problems.

subtopics.name: Impulse and resultant force
subtopics.detail: Impulse = Ft = Δ(mv). Resultant force = rate of change of momentum (F = Δp/Δt).

subtopics.name: Energy stores
subtopics.detail: Energy may be stored as kinetic, gravitational potential, chemical, elastic (strain), nuclear, electrostatic and internal (thermal).

subtopics.name: Energy transfers and conservation
subtopics.detail: Energy transferred by forces, electrical currents, heating and waves. Principle of conservation of energy; flow diagrams.

subtopics.name: Kinetic and gravitational potential energy
subtopics.detail: Ek = ½mv². Ep = mgh (change in gravitational PE).

subtopics.name: Work done
subtopics.detail: Mechanical and electrical work done equals energy transferred. W = Fd.

subtopics.name: Energy resources
subtopics.detail: How useful energy is obtained from fossil fuels, biofuels, water (waves, tides, hydro), geothermal, nuclear, solar cells and solar panels. Advantages and disadvantages: renewability, availability, reliability, scale, environmental impact. Solar radiation is the main source except geothermal, nuclear and tidal; energy released by nuclear fusion in the Sun.

subtopics.name: Power
subtopics.detail: Power = work done / time = energy transferred / time. P = W/t = E/t.

subtopics.name: Efficiency
subtopics.detail: Efficiency = (useful energy output / total energy input) × 100% or (useful power output / total power input) × 100%.

subtopics.name: Pressure definition and equation
subtopics.detail: Pressure = force / area (p = F/A). Everyday examples showing how pressure varies with force and area.

subtopics.name: Pressure in liquids
subtopics.detail: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth: Δp = ρgh.

subtopics.name: States of matter
subtopics.detail: Distinguishing properties of solids, liquids and gases. Terms for changes in state (melting, boiling, condensation, solidification).

subtopics.name: Particle model
subtopics.detail: Arrangement, separation and motion of particles in solids, liquids and gases. Forces and distances between particles affect properties.

subtopics.name: Brownian motion
subtopics.detail: Random motion of microscopic particles in suspension is evidence for the kinetic particle model. Explained by random collisions with gas or liquid molecules.

subtopics.name: Gas pressure and temperature
subtopics.detail: Gas pressure arises from particle collisions with surfaces. Qualitative effect of changing temperature (constant V) or changing volume (constant T).

subtopics.name: Absolute zero and the Kelvin scale
subtopics.detail: Absolute zero (−273 °C): particles have minimum kinetic energy. T (K) = θ (°C) + 273.

subtopics.name: Boyle's Law
subtopics.detail: pV = constant for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature. Graphical representation.

subtopics.name: Thermal expansion
subtopics.detail: Everyday applications and consequences of thermal expansion.

subtopics.name: Specific heat capacity
subtopics.detail: SHC = energy required per unit mass per unit temperature increase. E = mcθ. Experiments to measure SHC of a solid and a liquid.

subtopics.name: Melting and boiling
subtopics.detail: Melting and boiling involve energy input at constant temperature. Melting point and boiling point of water at standard pressure. Condensation and solidification described in terms of particles.

subtopics.name: Evaporation
subtopics.detail: Evaporation: more-energetic particles escape from a liquid surface, causing cooling. Factors affecting evaporation: temperature, surface area, air movement.

subtopics.name: Boiling vs. evaporation
subtopics.detail: Differences between boiling and evaporation. Cooling of an object in contact with an evaporating liquid.

subtopics.name: Conduction
subtopics.detail: Experiments demonstrating good and bad thermal conductors. Conduction in solids: lattice vibrations and free electrons in metals.

subtopics.name: Convection
subtopics.detail: Convection in liquids and gases: density changes drive the current. Experiments to illustrate convection.

subtopics.name: Radiation (infrared)
subtopics.detail: All objects emit infrared radiation. Transfer does not require a medium. Effect of surface colour and texture on emission, absorption and reflection.

subtopics.name: Good and bad emitters and absorbers
subtopics.detail: Experiments to distinguish good and bad emitters and absorbers. Rate of emission depends on surface temperature and area.

subtopics.name: Energy balance and Earth's temperature
subtopics.detail: Object at constant temperature transfers energy away at the same rate it receives it. Earth's temperature balance between incoming and outgoing radiation.

subtopics.name: Everyday applications
subtopics.detail: Basic and complex applications of conduction, convection and radiation: kitchen pans, room heating, car radiator, wood/coal fires.

subtopics.name: Energy transfer by waves
subtopics.detail: Waves transfer energy without transferring matter.

subtopics.name: Wave features
subtopics.detail: Wavefront, wavelength, frequency, crest, trough, amplitude and wave speed.

subtopics.name: Wave speed equation
subtopics.detail: v = fλ. Calculating wave speed, frequency or wavelength.

subtopics.name: Transverse and longitudinal waves
subtopics.detail: Transverse: vibration perpendicular to propagation (EM waves, water, S-waves). Longitudinal: vibration parallel to propagation (sound, P-waves).

subtopics.name: Reflection, refraction and diffraction
subtopics.detail: Waves undergo reflection (plane surface), refraction (change of speed) and diffraction (through a gap or past an edge). Ripple tank experiments.

subtopics.name: Diffraction effects
subtopics.detail: How wavelength and gap size affect diffraction through a gap; how wavelength affects diffraction at an edge.

subtopics.name: Reflection and plane mirrors
subtopics.detail: Laws of reflection (angle of incidence = angle of reflection). Image in a plane mirror: same size, same distance, virtual. Simple constructions for reflection.

subtopics.name: Refraction of light
subtopics.detail: Experiment showing refraction by transparent blocks. Passage of light through a transparent material at a boundary.

subtopics.name: Total internal reflection
subtopics.detail: Critical angle; internal reflection and total internal reflection. Everyday examples.

subtopics.name: Optical fibres
subtopics.detail: Use of optical fibres, particularly in telecommunications.

subtopics.name: Thin lenses
subtopics.detail: Converging and diverging lenses: focal length, principal axis, principal focus. Ray diagrams for real and virtual images. Image characteristics: enlarged/same size/diminished, upright/inverted, real/virtual.

subtopics.name: Magnifying glass and vision correction
subtopics.detail: Single converging lens as a magnifying glass. Converging and diverging lenses to correct long-sightedness and short-sightedness.

subtopics.name: Dispersion and colour
subtopics.detail: Dispersion of white light by a glass prism. Seven colours of the visible spectrum in order of frequency and wavelength. Monochromatic light.

subtopics.name: Refractive index
subtopics.detail: n = speed in medium 1 / speed in medium 2. Snell's law: n = sin i / sin r. Relationship to critical angle: n = 1/sin c.

topics.name: Electromagnetic spectrum
keywords: speed of light in a vacuum

subtopics.name: Regions of the EM spectrum
subtopics.detail: Main regions in order of frequency (and wavelength): radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-ray, gamma. All travel at the same speed in a vacuum (~3.0 × 10⁸ m/s).

subtopics.name: Uses of EM radiation
subtopics.detail: Radio: radio/TV/astronomy/RFID. Microwave: satellite TV, mobile phones, ovens. Infrared: grills, remote controls, thermal imaging, optical fibres. Visible: vision, photography. UV: security marking, detecting fake notes, sterilising water. X-rays: medical scanning, security. Gamma: sterilising food/equipment, cancer detection and treatment.

subtopics.name: Harmful effects of EM radiation
subtopics.detail: Microwaves: internal heating of cells. Infrared: skin burns. UV: skin cancer, eye damage. X-rays and gamma: cell mutation or damage.

subtopics.name: Communication systems
subtopics.detail: Satellite communication mainly by microwaves (low-orbit and geostationary). Mobile phones and wireless internet: microwaves. Bluetooth: radio waves. Optical fibres (visible light or infrared): cable TV and broadband.

subtopics.name: Digital vs. analogue signals
subtopics.detail: Difference between digital and analogue signals. Sound can be transmitted as either. Benefits of digital signalling: higher data rate, greater range due to accurate signal regeneration.

subtopics.name: Production and nature of sound
subtopics.detail: Sound produced by vibrating sources. Sound is a longitudinal wave requiring a medium. Compressions and rarefactions.

subtopics.name: Speed of sound
subtopics.detail: Speed of sound in air ≈ 330–350 m/s. Method: measuring distance and time. Sound travels faster in denser media.

subtopics.name: Loudness, pitch and amplitude
subtopics.detail: Amplitude affects loudness; frequency affects pitch. Audible range: 20 Hz to 20 000 Hz.

subtopics.name: Echoes
subtopics.detail: Echo = reflection of sound waves.

subtopics.name: Ultrasound
subtopics.detail: Ultrasound: frequency > 20 kHz. Uses: non-destructive material testing, medical scanning of soft tissue, sonar (depth/distance calculations).

subtopics.name: Magnetic poles and forces
subtopics.detail: Like poles repel; unlike poles attract. Force between magnets and magnetic materials. Induced magnetism.

subtopics.name: Magnetic and non-magnetic materials
subtopics.detail: Magnetic materials include iron, steel, nickel, cobalt. Non-magnetic materials do not experience magnetic forces.

subtopics.name: Temporary and permanent magnets
subtopics.detail: Soft iron: temporary magnets. Steel: permanent magnets. Uses of each.

subtopics.name: Magnetic fields and field lines
subtopics.detail: Magnetic field: region where a magnetic pole experiences a force. Drawing and plotting field lines around a bar magnet; direction = force on N pole. Field line spacing represents relative strength.

subtopics.name: Uses of magnets and electromagnets
subtopics.detail: Applications of permanent magnets and electromagnets. Magnetic forces arise from interactions between magnetic fields.

subtopics.name: Electric charge and static electricity
subtopics.detail: Positive and negative charges; like charges repel, unlike attract. Production of electrostatic charges by friction (transfer of electrons only). Detecting charges.

subtopics.name: Conductors and insulators
subtopics.detail: Experiment to distinguish conductors and insulators. Electron model: free electrons in conductors; bound electrons in insulators.

subtopics.name: Electric fields
subtopics.detail: Electric field: region where an electric charge experiences a force. Direction = force on a positive charge. Field patterns: around a point charge, a charged sphere, between parallel plates.

subtopics.name: Electric current
subtopics.detail: Current = charge / time (I = Q/t). Direct (d.c.) and alternating (a.c.) current. Conventional current from + to −; electron flow from − to +. Using ammeters (analogue and digital).

subtopics.name: Electromotive force and potential difference
subtopics.detail: e.m.f. = electrical work done by a source per unit charge around a complete circuit. p.d. = work done per unit charge through a component. Both measured in volts (V).

subtopics.name: Resistance and Ohm's Law
subtopics.detail: R = V/I. Experiment to determine resistance using voltmeter and ammeter. Current-voltage graphs for constant resistor, filament lamp and diode.

subtopics.name: Resistance and dimensions
subtopics.detail: For a metallic conductor: resistance ∝ length; resistance ∝ 1/cross-sectional area.

subtopics.name: Electrical power and energy
subtopics.detail: P = IV; E = IVt. Kilowatt-hour: kWh. Cost of electrical energy. Transfer of energy from source through circuit to surroundings.

subtopics.name: Circuit symbols and components
subtopics.detail: Drawing and interpreting circuit diagrams: cells, batteries, switches, resistors (fixed and variable), thermistors, LDRs, lamps, motors, bells, ammeters, voltmeters, transformers, fuses, relays, diodes, LEDs. Component behaviour.

subtopics.name: Series circuits
subtopics.detail: Current is the same at every point in a series circuit. Total e.m.f. is the sum of individual e.m.f.s. Total p.d. = sum of individual p.d.s. Combined series resistance = R₁ + R₂ + …

subtopics.name: Parallel circuits
subtopics.detail: Sum of currents into a junction = sum of currents leaving. p.d. is the same across all branches. Combined resistance of two parallel resistors is less than either alone. Advantages of parallel lamp circuits.

subtopics.name: Combining resistance
subtopics.detail: Combined resistance for resistors in series and in parallel (including calculation for two in parallel).

subtopics.name: Potential divider
subtopics.detail: How a variable potential divider works. Equation for two resistors as a potential divider: V₁/V₂ = R₁/R₂. p.d. across a conductor increases with resistance at constant current.

subtopics.name: Electrical hazards
subtopics.detail: Hazards: damaged insulation, overheating cables, damp conditions, overloading of plugs and extension leads.

subtopics.name: Mains wiring
subtopics.detail: Mains circuit: live wire, neutral wire and earth wire. Switch must be on the live side for safe disconnection.

subtopics.name: Fuses and circuit breakers
subtopics.detail: Operation of fuses and trip switches (circuit breakers). Choosing appropriate fuse ratings and trip settings.

subtopics.name: Double insulation and earthing
subtopics.detail: Outer casing must be non-conducting (double-insulated) or earthed. A fuse without an earth wire protects the cable for a double-insulated appliance.

subtopics.name: Electromagnetic induction
subtopics.detail: A conductor moving through a magnetic field, or a changing magnetic field linking a conductor, induces an e.m.f. Direction of induced e.m.f. opposes the change (Lenz's Law). Relative directions of force, field and induced current.

subtopics.name: Factors affecting induced e.m.f.
subtopics.detail: Magnitude of induced e.m.f. affected by speed of movement, strength of field and number of turns.

subtopics.name: The AC generator
subtopics.detail: Simple a.c. generator (rotating coil or magnet); slip rings and brushes. e.m.f. vs. time graph; relating coil position to peaks, troughs and zeros.

subtopics.name: Magnetic field of a current
subtopics.detail: Pattern and direction of magnetic field around straight wires and solenoids. Experiments to map fields. Qualitative variation of field strength; effect of changing current direction/magnitude. Applications: relays and loudspeakers.

subtopics.name: Force on a current-carrying conductor
subtopics.detail: Experiment showing force on a current in a magnetic field; effect of reversing current or field. Force on beams of charged particles in a magnetic field.

subtopics.name: The DC motor
subtopics.detail: Current-carrying coil in a field experiences a turning effect, increased by more turns, larger current or stronger field. DC motor operation: split-ring commutator and brushes.

subtopics.name: Transformers and voltage transformation
subtopics.detail: Construction: soft-iron core, primary and secondary coils. Step-up and step-down. Turns ratio equation: Vₚ/Vₛ = Nₚ/Nₛ. Transformer efficiency: VₚIₚ = VₛIₛ. P = I²R to explain why high voltage means lower power loss.

subtopics.name: High-voltage electricity transmission
subtopics.detail: Use of transformers in high-voltage transmission. Advantages: lower current reduces power loss in cables (P = I²R).

subtopics.name: Atomic structure
subtopics.detail: Atom: positively charged nucleus surrounded by orbiting electrons. Nucleus contains protons and neutrons.

subtopics.name: Protons, neutrons and electrons
subtopics.detail: Relative charges: proton +1, neutron 0, electron −1. Atoms form ions by gaining or losing electrons.

subtopics.name: Proton number and nucleon number
subtopics.detail: Proton (atomic) number Z; nucleon (mass) number A. Number of neutrons = A − Z. Nuclide notation ᴬZ X.

subtopics.name: Isotopes
subtopics.detail: Isotopes: atoms of the same element with the same proton number but different nucleon numbers.

subtopics.name: Alpha particle scattering
subtopics.detail: Scattering of α particles by a thin metal sheet provides evidence for a very small, dense, positively charged nucleus surrounded by mostly empty space.

subtopics.name: Nuclear fission and fusion
subtopics.detail: Fission: splitting of a heavy nucleus into smaller nuclei, releasing energy. Fusion: joining of light nuclei, releasing energy. Nuclide equations; qualitative mass-energy changes.

subtopics.name: Background radiation
subtopics.detail: Sources: radon gas, rocks and buildings, food and drink, cosmic rays. Measuring background and using it to correct count rates.

subtopics.name: Types of nuclear emission
subtopics.detail: Alpha (α), beta (β) and gamma (γ) radiation. Emission is spontaneous and random in direction.

subtopics.name: Properties of radiation
subtopics.detail: Deflection of α, β and γ in electric and magnetic fields. Relative ionising effects (kinetic energy and charge).

subtopics.name: Radioactive decay
subtopics.detail: Decay is a spontaneous, random change in an unstable nucleus. α or β emission changes the element. Decay equations using nuclide notation.

subtopics.name: Half-life
subtopics.detail: Half-life: time for half the nuclei of an isotope in any sample to decay. Simple calculations using tables or decay curves.

subtopics.name: Uses of radioactive isotopes
subtopics.detail: Smoke alarms, food irradiation, equipment sterilisation, thickness gauging, cancer diagnosis and treatment. Choice of isotope depends on radiation type and half-life.

subtopics.name: Radiation safety
subtopics.detail: Effects on living things: cell death, mutation, cancer. Safe handling, storage and transport of radioactive materials. Precautions: reduce exposure time, increase distance, use shielding.

subtopics.name: Earth's rotation and day/night
subtopics.detail: Earth rotates on its tilted axis approximately once every 24 hours, explaining apparent daily motion of the Sun and the cycle of day and night.

subtopics.name: Earth's orbit and the seasons
subtopics.detail: Earth orbits the Sun in approximately 365 days; the tilt explains the periodic cycle of seasons.

subtopics.name: The Moon's orbit and phases
subtopics.detail: The Moon orbits Earth in approximately one month, explaining the periodic cycle of lunar phases.

subtopics.name: The Solar System
subtopics.detail: The Solar System contains the Sun, eight named planets (and their order), dwarf planets, asteroids (asteroid belt), moons, comets and other natural satellites. Orbits are elliptical; the Sun is not at the centre of an ellipse.

subtopics.name: Gravitational fields in the Solar System
subtopics.detail: Sun contains most of the Solar System's mass; gravity keeps planets in orbit. Gravitational field strength at a planet's surface depends on its mass; field decreases with distance. Orbital speeds decrease with distance from the Sun. Objects in elliptical orbits travel faster when closer to the Sun (conservation of energy).

subtopics.name: Orbital speed and light travel time
subtopics.detail: Average orbital speed: v = 2πr/T. Calculating time for light to travel between Solar System objects.

subtopics.name: The Sun as a star
subtopics.detail: The Sun is a medium-sized star, mostly hydrogen and helium, radiating most energy as infrared, visible and ultraviolet. Stars are powered by nuclear fusion (hydrogen → helium).

subtopics.name: Life cycle of a star
subtopics.detail: Interstellar cloud → protostar → stable star (gravity balanced by outward thermal pressure) → red giant or red supergiant → planetary nebula/white dwarf (less massive) or supernova/neutron star/black hole (more massive). Supernova nebulae may form new star systems.

subtopics.name: Scale of the Universe
subtopics.detail: One light-year = 9.5 × 10¹⁵ m. The Milky Way is one of billions of galaxies; diameter ≈ 100 000 light-years.

subtopics.name: Redshift and the expanding Universe
subtopics.detail: Redshift: increase in observed wavelength from receding stars/galaxies. Light from distant galaxies is redshifted. This is evidence that the Universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang Theory.

subtopics.name: Cosmic microwave background radiation
subtopics.detail: CMBR: microwave radiation observed at all points in space, produced shortly after the Big Bang and stretched into the microwave region as the Universe expanded. Further evidence for the Big Bang.

subtopics.name: The Hubble constant and age of the Universe
subtopics.detail: Speed v of a galaxy found from its redshift. Distance d found from supernova brightness. Hubble constant H = v/d. 1/H estimates the age of the Universe — evidence that all matter was once at a single point.

topics.name: Electronics
topics.note: Old 0625 syllabus topic (dropped from 2026-2028 syllabus). Present in 2020-2024 papers.

subtopics.name: Analogue and digital signals
subtopics.detail: Difference between analogue and digital signals. Sound can be transmitted as either. Benefits of digital: higher data rate, greater range.

subtopics.name: Logic gates: AND, OR, NOT
subtopics.detail: Action of AND, OR and NOT gates; constructing truth tables for each.

subtopics.name: NAND and NOR gates
subtopics.detail: Action of NAND and NOR gates; truth tables.

subtopics.name: Combining logic gates
subtopics.detail: Producing truth tables for combinations of logic gates.

subtopics.name: Transistor as a switch
subtopics.detail: NPN transistor as a switch. Drawing and interpreting transistor switching circuits.

subtopics.name: Input sensors
subtopics.detail: Light-dependent resistor (LDR) as a light sensor; thermistor (NTC) as a temperature sensor in electronic circuits.

subtopics.name: Output devices
subtopics.detail: Output devices include LEDs, buzzers, relays and electric motors.
